0. 0.1 FOREWORD

)

This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 23 March 1984, after the draft finalized by the Treated Fabrics Sectional Committee had been approved by the Petroleum, Coal and Related Products Division Council. 0.2 Expanded vinyl coated fabrics are manuracturcd by applying on one side of a fabric a substantially contiliuous coating of suitably compounded polymer of vinyl chloride or a copolymer, the major constituent of which is vinyl chloride. During processing part of PVC coating is expanded. 0.3 This standard covers two types of material, namely, Type A and Type B depending on the base fabric used ( set 3.1 ). Further the two types shall have grades depending on the thickness of the coated material (.see 3.2 ). 0.4 The Committee was of the opinion that resistance to flame ( see 4.9 ) was an important requirement and the entire material being made in the However considering the present country should also pass this test. stage of the industry in the country anqalso the fact that this material is used in many non-critical uses, it was agreed to prescribe two classes of material, namely, Class A and Class B in the standard. Class B material is not recommended for applications where flame resisIn due course, the tance.is important from the safety point of view. Committee expects that with the development in the industry, the Class B material would be deleted from the standard. 0.4.1 In addition, revision: a) Requirement the fol]owing of flame modifications have been made and revised and in this

resistance

3.3 Classes - Both types and-ail grades of material shall be of two classes, Class A and Class B. Flame resistance test ( set 4.9 ) is required to be done in Class A material only. 4. REQUIREMENTS
- The expanded vinyl coated fabric shall consist of PVC polymer/copolymer composition which is either calendered and then laminated or is spread on to dyed;undyed base fabric. The intervening layer shall be expanded.
NOTE - The attention of users is drawn to the fact that the coated fabric may be damaged if wrong methods of cleaning are used. Furniture creams; dry cleaning solvents, pastes or waxes should not be used. For cleaning, only a soft cloth damped with soap and water or a mild detergent solution should be used. The surface should then be well rinsed with plain water and dried with a cloth.

4.2 Base Fabric - The base fabric shall be made or other synthetic fibre or their blends.

4.5 Colour, Grain and Finish -

The, colour, grain and finish of the material whether in single colour or multicolour effects, shall be as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. IS : 8698 - 1984 4.6 Resistance to Damage by Flexing - When tested by Method I ( De Mattia ) according to IS : 7016 ( Part 4 )-1973* the material shall comply with the number of flexing cycles given in Table 1. The material shall be considered to have complied with the requirements if none of the test pieces has shown signs of cracking to stage `D' after the first,stage and not more than half the test pieces have failed after the second stage of the test. For checking cracking to stage `D', the middle one-third portion which is folded with curvature outside shall be examined according to the foilowing method:

In case there is any doubt as to whether cracking has extended to the base i'abric, bend the flexed test specimen face outwards, round a glass rod 6 mm in diameter with a piece of filter paper between the test specimen and the rod. Brush a suitable coloured fluid, such as red ink containing 2 percent of a wetting agent over the flexed surface and regard the test ipecimen as cracked only if the ink stains the filter paper. 4.7 Gelling Test - Cur a sample specimen 250 mm long and 50 mm The sample specimen shall show no signs wide from the coated fabric. of cracking when it is folded double preferably around and aluminium plate or stainless steel plate about 2 mm thick and immersed for 30 seconds in a glass beaker containing acetone.

4.8.4 Colotrr Fastness to Light - The test pieces shall be subjected to colour fastness to daylight according to Appendix D of IS : 1259-1984". However, in case of any dispute the test specimens shall be subjected to accelerated fading test as stipulated in Appendix E of IS : 1259-1984*. For the purpose of this standard, the material shall be considered satisfactory when colour fastness of any test piece is rated not less than No. 4 of the standard pattern of plain dyed woollen fabrics as prescribed in IS : 686-1957t. Effects on printing may be observed in case of printed materials. 4.9 Flame Resistance ( for Class A only ) - The fabric shall be tested for flame resistance as described in Appendix H of IS : 1259-1984* and shall meet the following requirement.
4.9.1 The duration of flaming of the specimen 20 second after removal of the source of ignition.

4.10 Adhesion of Coating - The plies in any of the test pieces taken for test shall not separate more than 10 mm under a load of 27.5 N len tested as prescribed in Appendix J of IS : 1259.1984*. IS:8698-1984 5.2 Test Specimens - `Test pieces shall be cut from the samples in the required number and in appropriate manner as specified in the individual methods of test and in accordance with Appendix B. $2.1 In case where less than 1 metre sample is to be tested the number of test specimens may be reduced at the discretion of the purchaser. 6. PACKING, MARKING, AND STORAGE NUMBER OF CUTS IN THE ROLL

6.1 Packing - `I'he material shall be securely packed in the form of a roll so as to ensure safe transportation. 6.2 The material shall be in rolls of minimum 15 metres lengths. Short lengths of less than 15 metres shall be permitted but the number of such short length shall be not more than one per roll. Further no short length shall be less than 5 metres in length. In any consignment not more than 10 percent of rolls shall contain short lengths. 6.3 Marking roll with: a) b) c) d) 6.3.1 The material shall be marked at the outer end of each

the manufacturer's name or trade-mark, if any; grade and type of material; month and year of manufacture; and length of mslterial in metres. The material may also be marked with the Standard Mark.

Nom - `Ike use of the Standard Mark ia governed by the provisions of the Bureauof Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of anditions under which a liccncs for the we of tha Standard Mark may be granted to mrnufactwen or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.

6.4 Storage - The expanded vinyl coated fabric shall be stored vertically on a clean; dry, firm*and level surface in well ventilated place not exposed to direct sunlight and protected from dust', moisture, corrosive and solvent fumes. 7. SAMPLING 7.1 Sampling 7.1.1 Lot - In any consignment, all the rolls of expanded vinyl coated fabric of the same type, grade, colour and finish shall be grouped together and each such group shall constitute a lot. 9 AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY

7.2 Number of Tests 7.2.1 Each of the lengths obtained from a lot shall be examined for visual defects, and coating, and if found satisfactory, further tests as specified shall be carried out. 7.2.2 From each of the rolls selected according to 7.1.2 one metre length of expanded vinyl coated fabric shall be cut, care being taken to exclude not less than 0.25 m length of fabric from either end. The test specimens necessary for the various tests specified in the standard shall be cut from the lengths of expanded vinyl coated fabric thus obtained. All the samples shall be kept out of contact from one another or any other material that may cause contamination. Scheme of selection of test specimens from the sample length is given in Fig. 1. 7.3 Criteria for Conformity

7.3.1 The lot shall `be declared as conforming to the specification for various characteristics referred in 4 if for each of the characteristics the test results on all individual specimens are found to be within limits of the specification. or 7.3.2 If the specimen, taken from a one metre length, fails in one For this purpose, more tests, each such test shall be repeated twice.

APPENDIX ( C~UZLM 3.2 j
DETERMINATION A-l. APPARATUS

.A

OF THICKNESS

A-l.1 Gauge - The gauge shall be of dead-weight type, equippccl with a dial graduated to read directly to 0.02 mm. The presser foot shall be ci: cular having a diameter of 9.5 f 092 mm or 50 `i OS05 mm. The press"r foot and connected moving parts shall be loaded to give the pressure according to the category of articles being measured. The presser foot and anvil surfaces shall be plane to within 0,002 mm, and parallel to one another to within 0'002 mm. The gauge shal1 be calibrated for the actual load exerted by the presser foot by means of any device so arranged as to measure the total force exerted by the presser foot at the several gauge readings or presser foot levels selected for calibration. The presser foot shall be brought to each calibration levrl from a higher one.

oblique line drawn at at a distance of about five evenly distributed between 50 and 150

A-2.2 Place the coated fabric on the anvil of the gauge, smoothen it but without tension. Lower the presser foot on to the material ( without impact ), allow it to rest for 10 seconds, obscrvc and record the reading of the dial. _---

IS : 8698 - 1984 - Express the results in millimetres. A-2.3 Expremion of Results The mean thickness in millimetres is the arithmetic mean of the .five measured values on the same oblique line.

METHOD B-l. METHOD OF SELECTION OF TEST SPECIMENS

B-l.1 The test specimens shall be selected from one metre sample of full width, when it is laid on a flat rigid surface with fabric side uppermost without any tension in either direction. B-l.2 Draw the line for `test specimens over the sample as laid in B-1.1, in accordance with Fig. 1 which shows the position of thti specified numbers of specimens for each test.
